# Getting started with Z.ai: a beginner's guide to the free chatbot

> **In short:** Z.ai is a chatbot you use in a web browser at chat.z.ai, and it runs on the company's GLM models. You can start with a simple question in minutes. The most important thing to know: it can sound confident while being wrong, so check anything important.

This guide is for anyone who has heard about AI chatbots and wants a calm, first look at one. By the end, you'll have opened Z.ai, asked a real question, improved the answer, and learned what not to type into it. No technical background is needed.

## Before you start
- **A device with a web browser.** A phone, tablet, or computer works. You don't need to install anything.
- **An email address you can check**, in case the site asks you to sign up or sign in. Whether an account is required can change, so follow what the site asks.
- **About 20 minutes** for the whole guide.

## Step 1 — Open chat.z.ai and look around
Open your browser, type **chat.z.ai** into the address bar, and press Enter. You should see an empty chat with a message box at the bottom of the screen. This box is where you type. Chat assistants like this one work like a very fast, very patient text conversation: you type a message, and the reply appears below it.

Take a moment to look at the rest of the page. You may see a sidebar with past conversations, a button to start a new chat, and a menu for settings. Don't worry about any of it yet. If you're asked to sign in or create an account, follow the on-screen steps and use an email address you check often. If the page looks different from this description, look for the message box first, because that's the one thing you need.

💬 Example: You don't need to type anything yet. Just find the message box.

You'll know it worked when you can see a place to type your message and the page has loaded without errors.

## Step 2 — Check which model you're using
Z.ai is built on what it calls its GLM models. "Model" is simply the name for the AI engine behind the chat. Think of it like a car engine: the same dashboard can sometimes sit on different engines, and each one handles tasks a little differently. Some sites let you choose a model from a menu near the top of the chat or near the message box.

If you see a model menu, tap or click it and look at what's available. Model names and options can change over time, so don't rely on a name from this guide or someone else's article. If you don't see a menu, that's fine; the default model will still answer your questions. Pick the option that's labeled as the general or everyday choice if you're unsure.

💬 Example: Not applicable here. You're just checking what's on screen.

You'll know it worked when you've either picked a model from the menu or confirmed that no menu is shown and you're ready to type.

## Step 3 — Ask your first question
Click inside the message box, type a question in ordinary language, and press Enter, or tap the send arrow next to the box. Write as if you're talking to a helpful friend. A few seconds later, the reply should start appearing below your message, a few words at a time.

Start with something simple that you already know the answer to, so you can judge the reply yourself. Good first questions are about everyday topics. Remember: the assistant cannot see your screen, your files, or the live internet unless the site specifically offers those features. It answers from patterns it learned during training, so it can be wrong.

💬 Example: "Explain the difference between a sprain and a strain in simple words, and give me two examples of each, using [your hobby] as the example."

If the reply is very short or seems to ignore your question, press the button to start a new chat and try again with more detail.

You'll know it worked when a written answer appears below your message and it relates to the question you asked.

## Step 4 — Improve the answer with a follow-up
The first answer is rarely the best one. The easiest way to improve it is to reply in the same chat, the way you'd continue talking with a person. The assistant remembers what you said earlier in that conversation, so you can ask it to adjust, shorten, or explain differently. Click in the message box below its reply and type your follow-up.

Be specific about what you want. Saying "make it simpler" or "give me three bullet points" helps much more than "try again." If the reply still misses the point, rephrase your original question with more detail about who the answer is for.

💬 Example: "That's helpful, but I'm a complete beginner. Please rewrite it in five short sentences and avoid medical or technical words."

You'll know it worked when the new reply matches the change you asked for, such as being shorter, simpler, or in a different format.

## Step 5 — Try a practical task
Now try something useful for your daily life. Chatbots are good at drafting, organizing, and explaining. For example, you can ask for help writing a polite message, planning a simple schedule, or making a shopping list from a recipe. The assistant can draft the text, but it can't send emails, book appointments, or make purchases for you. You still copy the result and use it yourself.

If you want the assistant to work with a longer piece of text, such as a paragraph from a letter you received, paste it into the message box. Only paste text you're comfortable sharing, and remove names, account numbers, and addresses first.

💬 Example: "Help me write a short, friendly reminder to a neighbor about returning my ladder. Keep it under 60 words and end with a thank-you."

You'll know it worked when the assistant gives you a draft you can read, copy, and edit before using it anywhere else.

## Step 6 — Decide what to keep private
This step matters more than any other. Treat a chatbot like a public postcard: anything you type could be stored, reviewed under the company's rules, or seen by someone who gets access to your account. Z.ai has its own privacy policy, and different AI companies handle stored conversations differently, so read the policy on the official site before sharing anything personal. Look for the section on how long chats are kept and how to delete them.

As a simple rule, don't type passwords, bank or card numbers, Social Security numbers, medical records, or other people's private details. For a sensitive document, use a short summary or a made-up version instead. Also check whether your account has a way to clear your chat history, and use it if you're on a shared computer.

💬 Example: Instead of pasting a real bill, try: "Here is a made-up bill for a [service type] with a $[amount] charge. Explain in simple terms what each line might mean."

You'll know it worked when you've read the privacy section, know where to delete past chats, and have a personal rule for what stays out of the message box.

## Common mistakes
- **Trusting every answer.** Chatbots can state wrong facts with confidence. Fix it by checking important details, such as dates, rules, or health and money information, with an official source or a qualified professional.
- **Sharing too much too soon.** Beginners often paste whole documents or personal details. Fix it by removing names, numbers, and addresses before you paste anything.
- **Giving up after one reply.** A vague first answer doesn't mean the tool is useless. Fix it by asking a follow-up with a clear instruction, like "shorter" or "for a beginner."

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You can use Z.ai to explain a confusing letter, plan a weekend meal, or draft a message to a friend. Ask it to explain things in plain words, then double-check anything that matters.
- **For your business or work:** You can ask it to outline a meeting agenda, rewrite a paragraph for clarity, or brainstorm names for a project. Keep client, employee, and company information out of the chat unless your employer has approved the tool for that use.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with low-stakes questions and drafts. Build the habit of checking the answer and protecting your personal details. That habit matters more than any single feature.

## Try it now
Open **chat.z.ai** in your browser, find the message box, and type this: "Give me three simple tips for starting a new hobby, written for a complete beginner." Read the reply, then send one follow-up asking it to make the tips shorter. Two minutes is all it takes.
